Answer: B
Reason: The recurrent, non-resolving retrocardiac opacity seen in Figure 1 that clears in Figures 2 and 3 is characteristic of a pulmonary sequestration, which often presents as persistent or recurrent lower lobe consolidation due to its anomalous systemic arterial supply and poor drainage. This congenital anomaly explains the "recurrent" nature better than an abscess (which would typically show cavitation), effusion (which would layer differently), or pneumonia (which usually resolves completely).
